newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand postpones limits on bank offshore loans.
newsitem.headline: Thailand postpones limits on bank offshore loans.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand said on Thursday it had decided to postpone new measures to limit the amount of foreign loans that offshore units of foreign and local banks can import for relending in the domestic market.

"We have decided to postpone the planned measures and review the whole situation again at the end of this year," Thirachai Phuvanatnaranubala, director of the central bank's financial institutions supervision and development department, told Reuters.

The central bank in early October issued guidelines to foreign and local banks that would have limited out-in loans brought into Thailand by their offshore units under the Bangkok International Banking Facility (BIBF).
Out-in loans refer to foreign funds that offshore banks import for relending to local clients.
The measures were due to come into effect during the September-December period but banks had lobbied the central bank for a delay.
The measures, aimed at curbing short-term foreign fund inflows into Thailand, alarmed investors in the stock exchange and caused the market to plummet.
Thirachai said the postponement was made after banks had asked the central bank for more time to adjust their portfolios to meet the new guidelines.
"We have to go through a lot more discussion on this. But we are still concerned about the level of foreign borrowings," he said.
The central bank would wait until the end of this year when the net Thai foreign and private sector borrowing picture was clearer to decide on the future of the measures, Thirachai said.

Among the measures outlined by the central bank was that the rise of out-in loans extended by offshore units of local banks during September-December this year would be limited to seven percent of the increase of baht-denominated loans they lend out over the same period.
The central bank also said it would raise to $US5 million from $2 million the minimum out-in loans that licensed offshore banking units could extend to new local clients.

It had added that the ratio of out-in loans to local baht-denominated loans granted by the offshore BIBF units of existing foreign banks' branches during September-December would be limited at the ratio of 1 to 1.
